items.title: Foreign driving licence not valid in India without local authorisation: P&H High Court
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court recently declined to rely on a man's foreign driving licence to exonerate him from his liability in a road accident case [Sameer Gaba v Priyanka & Others] Justice Deepak Gupta noted that Section 3 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 prohibits a person from driving a motor vehicle in a public place unless he holds an effective driving licence authorising him to drive that vehicle. Hence, a foreign driving licence will not be automatically valid in India unless it is endorsed by an Indian authority, the Court said in its verdict of September 7. "A foreign driving licence does not, merely because it is valid in the country of its issuance, automatically confer a right upon its holder to drive a motor vehicle in India," the Court added. The Court was hearing an appeal filed by the driver against an order of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT) at Kurukshetra. The MACT had allowed the concerned insurance company to recover the compensation amount paid by it to a road accident victim's family from the driver who did not possess a valid driving licence in India. items.title: TN: Parents of teenage boy allege honour killing, police say it was death by drowning
items.summary: A 16-year-old boy was found dead in a kammoi (waterbody) in Madurai’s Koodal Pudur on September 6. Initial reports said the child’s family has alleged an honour killing. Police sources TNM spoke to, however, insist that this is a case of accidental drowning. The family has alleged that the boy was killed because he was in touch with a girl from another community. Both are from different intermediate castes. Police sources also told TNM that the boy’s parents have refused to accept his body unless a murder case is registered. According to sources, the boy and his friends had gone swimming in the kammoi. CCTV footage from the area allegedly shows them attempting to use styrofoam sheets as flotation devices when the boy went underwater. When the boy’s friends were unable to pull him out, they panicked and eventually fled the scene, sources said. The boy’s parents registered a missing person’s complaint on September 5, and his body was recovered from the kammoi on September 6, police said. Additionally, the postmortem report has not shown any proof of violence and is consistent with signs of accidental drowning, sources further said.
